// simple graphics demo showing hypocycloids: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypocycloid

import vec
import color
import gl

fatal(gl.window("hypocycloid", 1024, 768))

while gl.frame():
    if gl.button("escape") == 1: return
    gl.clear(color_black)
    gl.translate(float(gl.window_size()) / 2.0)
    gl.scale(gl.window_size().y / 4.0)
    let scalechange = sin(gl.time() * 50.0) * 0.2
    let pts = map(360 * 4 + 1) a:
        fold(5, float2_0) p, i:
            p + sincos(a / 4.0 * pow(3.0, i)) * pow(0.4 + scalechange, i)
    gl.line_mode 1:
        gl.polygon(pts)

// simple graphics demo showing euler spirals:
// http://blog.matthen.com/post/67889183164/draw-a-straight-line-and-then-continue-it-for-the

import vec
import color
import gl
import utilui

fatal(gl.window("euler spiral", 1024, 768))

let pts = [ float2_0, float2_x ]
var angle = 0.0

let szv = scrollzoomview {
    rate: 1.3,
    mins: 5,
    defaults: 10,
    maxs: 22,
    buttonname: "mouse1"
}

while gl.frame():
    if gl.button("escape") == 1: return
    gl.clear(color_black)
    let scale, panoffset = szv.update(float2_1 * -50.0, float2_1 * 50.0, gl.window_size())
    gl.scale(scale)
    gl.translate(panoffset)
    if pts.length < 10000:
        angle += 2.0 + (rnd_float() - 0.5) / 20.0
        let a = atan2(pts.top - pts[pts.length - 2])
        pts.push(pts.top + sincos(a + angle))
    gl.line_mode 1:
        gl.polygon(pts)

/* random maze pattern inspired on this C64 basic program:

10 PRINT CHR$ (205.5 + RND (1)); : GOTO 10

Sadly, even lobster can't compete with that conciseness :)
http://10print.org/

*/

import vec
import color
import gl

fatal(gl.window("rndmaze", 1024, 768))

def endcap_line(pts, thickness):
    gl.line(pts[0], pts[1], thickness)
    for pts: gl.translate _: gl.circle(thickness / 2.0, 40)

while gl.frame():
    if gl.button("escape") == 1: return
    gl.clear(color_black)
    rnd_seed(0)
    let scale = gl.window_size().y / 25
    gl.scale(scale)
    forxy(gl.window_size() / scale + 1) v:
        gl.translate v:
            if rnd(3):   // this is not in the original, and adds some blank spaces.. comment this line out if needed
                endcap_line(if rnd(2): [ float2_0, float2_1 ]
                                 else: [ float2_x, float2_y ], 0.25)

import vec
import color
import gl

let size = 32

gl.window("Animated Binary Number", size * 9, size * 24)
gl.set_font_name("data/fonts/US101/US101.ttf")

var n = 0

while gl.frame():
    if gl.button("escape") == 1: return
    gl.clear(color_black)
    gl.color(color_white)
    gl.translate float2_1 * size
    gl.set_font_size(size * 2)
    gl.text("{n}")
    gl.translate float2_x * 6.0 * size:
        gl.text(number_to_string(n, 16 /* HEX */, 0))
    gl.set_font_size(size)
    gl.translate float2_y * 3.0 * size
    for(64) b:
        gl.translate float2_y * size * b:
            guard n & (1 << b)
            gl.color((color { b & 1, (b & 2) >> 1, (b & 4) >> 2, 1.0 } + color_white) * 0.5)
            gl.text("{b}")
            gl.translate float2_x * size
            gl.translate float2_1 * 0.5 * size:
                gl.circle(size * 0.5, 20)
            gl.translate float2_x * 1.5 * size
            gl.text("{1 << b}")
            gl.translate float2_x * 3.5 * size
            gl.text(number_to_string(1 << b, 16 /* HEX */, 0))
    n++

// graphics demo showing an animated "tree of pythagoras"

import vec
import color
import gl

let poly_verts = []
let poly_meshes = []

def branch(n, max, scale, len) -> void:
    if n == poly_meshes.length:
        let poly = [ float2_x, -float2_x, float2 { -scale, len }, float2 { scale, len } ]
        poly_verts.push(poly)
        poly_meshes.push(gl.new_poly(poly))
    gl.color(color { n / max, 0.8, n / max, 1.0 })
    gl.render_mesh(poly_meshes[n])
    gl.color(color { 0.3, 0.1, 0.0, 0.7 })
    for(2) i:
        gl.line(poly_verts[n][i], poly_verts[n][3 - i], 0.2)
    guard n < max
    gl.translate(float2 { 0.0, len })
    gl.scale(scale)
    for(2) i:
        gl.rotate_z(sincos((i * 2.0 - 1.0) * 30.0 + sin(gl.time() * 50.0) * n + rnd(40) - 20.0)):
            branch(n + 1, max, scale, len + 0.5)

fatal(gl.window("Pythagoras tree in Lobster", 1024, 768))

while gl.frame():
    if gl.button("escape") == 1: return
    gl.clear(color_grey)
    rnd_seed(0)
    gl.translate(float(gl.window_size()) / float2 { 2.0, 1.0 })
    gl.rotate_z(float2 { -1.0, 0.0 })
    gl.scale(gl.window_size().y / 17.0)
    branch(0, 11.0, 0.7, 4)

// example of how to play wav files

import std
import vec
import color
import gl

fatal(gl.window("wav sound test", 1024, 768))
check(gl.set_font_name("data/fonts/Carrois_Gothic_SC/CarroisGothicSC-Regular.ttf") and
      gl.set_font_size(30),
      "can\'t load font!")

let audio_freq = 44100
let sine = play_audio_stream(audio_freq, 1, 10)
let sine_freq = 440.0
let sine_vol = 0.5
var sine_t = 0.0
var stream_avail = 0.0
def sine_queue_secs(time):
    guard stream_avail < time
    let remaining = time - stream_avail
    let sample_count = int(audio_freq * remaining)
    let samples = map(sample_count):
        sine_t += 1.0 / float(audio_freq)
        sine_vol * sin(sine_t * sine_freq * 360.0)
    put_audio_stream(sine, samples)
    stream_avail += remaining

while gl.frame():
    if gl.button("escape") == 1: return
    gl.clear(color_black)
    gl.color(color_white)
    gl.text("left mouse to shoot rifle, right mouse for shotgun, space for sine wave")
    if gl.button("mouse1") == 1:
        check(play_wav("data/sounds/awesund/rifle.wav"), "can\'t load sound!")
    if gl.button("mouse3") == 1:
        check(play_wav("data/sounds/awesund/shotgun.wav"), "can\'t load sound!")

    stream_avail = max(stream_avail - gl.delta_time(), 0.0)
    if gl.button("space") >= 1:
        sine_queue_secs(0.2)
